title: Quantum sampling in hybrid light-matter systems with mixed statistics
authors: Franziska Barkhausen, Laura Ares, Stefan Schumacher, Jan Sperling
abstract: Boson sampling is one of the most prominent methods to verify quantum advantage, harnessing the computational complexity of the permanent of a network matrix. Similar quantum sampling problems utilize other expressions for the output probabilities, such as the fermion-based analog applying determinants. In this work, we study sampling setups of interacting light-matter systems, combining fermion and boson sampling. The mixed network input consists of fermionic and bosonic excitations. Sampling the output probability of the modes then yields contributions that are neither purely determinant nor permanent but general immanants. Specifically, we prove that these immanant contributions are linearly independent from determinants and permanents, rendering our mixed sampling network an ideal candidate for light-matter quantum application beyond pure fermion and boson sampling. Furthermore, quantum sampling with statistics that are neither bosonic nor fermionic results in expressions which even exceed immanants, further extending the functionality of quantum samplers.
summary: This paper develops a mathematical framework to analyze quantum sampling in hybrid light-matter systems combining fermionic and bosonic excitations. It shows that the resulting output probabilities are described by generalized matrix immanants, which are mathematically distinct from simple determinants or permanents. This demonstrates that such mixed-statistics systems enable computational functionalities beyond what is achievable with pure bosonic or fermionic quantum circuits.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum sampling in hybrid light-matter systems where the statistics of excitations are mixed (fermionic and bosonic), moving beyond standard boson or fermion sampling.
main_result: The output probabilities are governed by generalized matrix immanants, which are proven to be linearly independent from standard determinants and permanents, indicating novel computational resources.
method: The analysis uses the Born rule applied to the output state derived from a unitary linear transformation acting on mixed fermionic and bosonic operators, leading to the definition of generalized immanants.
model_or_system: The model involves interacting light-matter systems described by a linear network transformation acting on fermionic and bosonic excitations. The complexity is analyzed by generalizing the mathematical structure beyond simple commutation relations.
key_observables: The output probability $p$, which is proportional to the square of the generalized immanant, $|	ext{imm}(A)|^2$.
important_parameters: The structure of the immanant depends on the exchange symmetries encoded by the function $\chi(\sigma)$, which can be an irreducible character of $S_N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes single excitations per output mode and focuses on the operator part of the output state, neglecting higher-excitation terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sampling network for mixed modes and plot the decomposition coefficients of the resulting immanant into contributions from determinants, permanents, and residual components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the mathematical framework using immanants, then applying it to mixed fermionic/bosonic systems, and finally extending the analysis to quasiparticle sampling, showing the resulting functions exceed standard immanant forms.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the mathematical complexity of quantum computation in realistic, mixed-statistics physical platforms, providing a rigorous framework for quantifying quantum advantage beyond established models.
